races.name: Norfolk Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Agamemnon
runners_data.note: A six-lengths winner on debut at Sandown and runner-up at Royal Ascot last season, this is a horse with a live chance but its naturally prominent style is crowded out in this field, meaning Oisin Murphy will have to adapt and accept a position he would not naturally choose; the higher-class form is the draw here, not the pace map placement.
runners_data.comment: Bolted up in a novice at Wolverhampton last time by three lengths, but that form needs boosting further as this is a significant step up in class; bred for speed and effective at today's trip, but ranked 18th of 21 on our figures, making this a tough ask from stall 1.

runners_data.name: Blake's Monarch
runners_data.note: Ran respectably for second at Sandown latest, trainer Ivan Furtado operating at 1/35 over the past fortnight which is a concern; this runner wants to race prominently but with so many rivals ahead of it in the queue for those positions, De Sousa may find the horse racing more keenly than ideal in a compressed midfield.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Blake's Monarch looks out of its depth stepping up in class here, despite showing fair form on turf debut at Chester 21 days ago and proven effectiveness at the trip on good ground.

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partner for Aidan O'Brien, this colt has three runs under his belt and a smart profile including a win at Cork — the most experienced and exposed of the O'Brien two-year-olds here; races prominently and with Moore able to slide into a forward slot from the widening field, a clean run could mean this is one prominent type who actually gets its position.
runners_data.comment: Carry The Flag arrives here on the back of a fine Group 3 second at The Curragh, beaten just a length and a quarter while stepping up in class and showing sharp early pace; a big, strong type with a top jockey aboard, the five furlongs here may actually bring out the best in this high-class prospect.

runners_data.name: El Floridita
runners_data.note: A flashy five-furlong winner at Carlisle latest, Rowan Scott takes the ride for Nigel Tinkler whose 14-day strike rate of 0/23 is modest; El Floridita naturally wants to race close to the pace but in this field the draw and sheer numbers mean it is realistically likely to be shuffled back further than suits.
runners_data.comment: Showed improved form when taking a maiden at Redcar last time, but that win came with caveats and this represents a sharp step up in grade for a recent purchase. Drawn 8, handles today's trip and conditions, yet ranks 16th of 21 on our figures — hard to get excited.

runners_data.name: Flight Signal
runners_data.note: James Doyle on this Archie Watson-trained winner of his only start at Newmarket, strong on paper — Watson strike rate of 0/31 over 14 days is a flag though Doyle is a strong compensating factor; wants to race prominently but with the field this congested, getting a forward berth may require Doyle to push early, which risks burning energy before the turn.
runners_data.comment: Burst clear by three-and-a-quarter lengths on debut at Bath, Flight Signal looks a promising type who acts on this going and trip, though stepping up sharply in class from a novice on just one start is the obvious query at a mark of 129lb from stall 6.

runners_data.name: Force Noir
runners_data.note: A winner on debut at Catterick and second at Chester, wearing a hood and trained by Kevin Philippart De Foy whose 14-day figures are modest at 1/19; 54 days since last run adds a question mark, and this runner is naturally prominent yet displayed in a hold-up slot purely because the field's prominent contingent is over-subscribed — treat this as a horse likely to travel forward regardless of map position.
runners_data.comment: Blinkers fitted for the first time as Force Noir returns after a 54-day break, and that Naas maiden win — striding clear by 4¼ lengths on better ground — showed a willing attitude with more to come; the trip and track look suitable, though stall 19 and 129 lb are worth noting.

runners_data.name: Mr Macartney
runners_data.note: Form reads 4176 over five and six furlongs, so inconsistency is a concern despite a Redcar win in the sequence; wearing a visor for Oli Rix, this horse wants to be close to the pace but recent form suggests vulnerability at this level — the visor is a small positive but the hold-up slot here purely reflects field overcrowding, not a genuine style shift.
runners_data.comment: Beaten two lengths in a Listed contest at Sandown 23 days ago, Mr Macartney has course-and-distance form to his name and steps up in trip wearing a visor for the first time, which could unlock improvement — though his recent sixth and seventh suggest he's yet to recapture that winning thread.

runners_data.name: Mussab
runners_data.note: Ran third on debut at the Curragh over six furlongs, lightly raced with an unknown style tag and Colin Keane in the saddle for the powerful Fahey stable; the drop to five furlongs is an unknown factor on a form string of just one run, and Keane will need to find out if the speed is there early.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise on debut, finishing third beaten just 1¼ lengths at York in novice company, and Mussab clearly handles today's trip and good ground well enough — but the step up in class is a concern, and greenness under pressure could be costly again from stall 14.

runners_data.name: New Yorker
runners_data.note: The most genuine hold-up type in this field for O'Brien, with a career form of 1-3-4 and two placed efforts over five furlongs at the Curragh on similar ground; Wayne Lordan knows the horse and if the pace is strong enough this is the one closest to a true sit-and-finish profile in the race, wearing a hood to help settle.
runners_data.comment: Hooded for the first time and steadily building through recent starts, but ranked 15th of 21 on our figures and the speed rating of 33 makes this a tough ask; sprint-bred and effective over today's trip on good ground, though this looks a step too far at present.

runners_data.name: Orthodox
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's one-race winner for Rossa Ryan, an impressive debut winner over five at Windsor on Good — this is the horse who looked electric on debut and Cox knows how to place two-year-olds at this level; genuinely prominent style and may be one of the horses who actually secures that position given the trainer/jockey combination.
runners_data.comment: Impressive on debut, winning a Salisbury maiden by 2½ lengths on good ground over today's trip, but that's just one run to go on; bred for speed and thought highly of, though stall 16 and a 37-day absence from a lightly raced sort introduce some uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Persian Spring
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner for Jamie Spencer — an intriguing combination given Spencer's tendency to find a path even in crowded fields; won over six at Newmarket then fifth over five, the drop back to five may be the test here though the form is solid and Spencer's race-reading could be the edge.
runners_data.comment: Successful over today's trip and going when landing a York novice last time out, Persian Spring enters from stall 10 carrying 129 lb, though the step back in distance raises a question — better may yet come, but the trip could blunt that progress.

runners_data.name: Savage Mariner
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partner for Hugo Palmer, ran second over six furlongs at Haydock on debut and is a midfield type placed into a hold-up slot on this map because of field congestion rather than genuine inclination; lightly raced with an unknown style tag — treat as a runner whose exact role is genuinely uncertain and whose chance depends on Marquand's in-running decision.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise on debut, going down by just 1½ lengths at Leicester, and the step back to 6f looks a natural fit — though the drop in trip isn't guaranteed to unlock improvement. Carries 129 lb from stall 20 yet to score, but there's potential here.

runners_data.name: Social Symbol
runners_data.note: William Buick on a Simon and Ed Crisford-trained winner of his only start over five at Goodwood — the Crisford yard has been quiet over 14 days at 0/23 but Buick's presence and the horse's natural speed over five could see it push forward and actually hold a prominent position given its gate speed.
runners_data.comment: Sole start produced a half-length debut win at Ripon 17 days ago — form since franked and scope for improvement stepping up in class, but ranked 19th of 21 on our figures here, making this a significant jump from novice company at stall 18 carrying 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Glory
runners_data.note: Jason Watson rides this Charles Hills-trained horse, whose form on Firm going reads 1-3 — both runs on Firm rather than Good To Firm, so the going difference is a minor but real flag; wants to race prominently and the fact this runner has only faced Firm ground means the slight ease in conditions is an unknown.
runners_data.comment: Beaten on debut before getting off the mark in a Bath novice last time — overcoming a slow start and trouble in running to score by 2½l — Sovereign Glory arrives 39 days later with a case for progressing further, and the 5-6f trip on fast ground suits; but ranked 20 of 21 on our figures, stall 17 and 129lb make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Star Prospect
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle on Joseph O'Brien's runner, who has placed third and won over five on Good and Soft respectively — the softer going win raises a small question over how it handles genuinely quick ground today; naturally prominent and McMonagle is one of the most in-form young jockeys around, which is a significant positive in a crowded field.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win before finishing a staying-on third at Naas last time, Star Prospect looks to have more improvement in the locker and takes well to this trip and varied ground; the 129 lb burden from stall 7 is the one query.

runners_data.name: Tribeca
runners_data.note: Donagh O'Connor on this Robson De Aguiar-trained runner who won over six furlongs at Newmarket on debut — stepping down to five today is a significant question mark, as the trip reduction asks for a different kind of speed; 56 days since last ran is the longest absence in the field and De Aguiar is 1/11 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Tribeca took his debut maiden at Navan in authoritative fashion, always holding sway throughout, but returns here after 56 days off and faces a step up in class; effective at today's trip and suited by sounder ground, this promising colt has the tools but remains unexposed.

runners_data.name: Underdog
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's eight-day turnaround after winning at Sandown suggests confidence — the freshness angle is real but so is the concern about a quick reappearance in a Group 2 off a maiden win; Saffie Osborne takes a big-race opportunity and the horse won over five on Good which at least ticks the surface and distance boxes.
runners_data.comment: Debut winner at Sandown, beating more experienced rivals with a sharp turn of foot, but stepping up considerably in class here and our figures rank it 17th of 21; the in-form trainer and speedy pedigree offer slim encouragement, yet this looks a tough ask on ratings.

runners_data.name: Where Love Lives
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's two-time five-furlong winner at Thirsk and Pontefract, unbeaten in two starts — this is the confirmed front-runner in the race and Kevin Stott will aim to control from the outset; the key question is whether this horse, whose two wins came in smaller fields, can replicate that front-running role when breaking from a wide draw in a 21-runner sprint.
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in its last two starts, Where Love Lives is a big, powerful type still maturing and looks to have more improvement in the locker after taking Listed honours at Sandown last time; the slight hesitation before finding top gear is the one concern to keep in mind.

runners_data.name: Ez Tina
runners_data.note: Wesley Ward's first-string female American invader wearing a hood, with US form that reads well on paper but completely unknown on British turf; Juan Hernandez takes the ride and the going flag is UNKNOWN, meaning this runner is a genuine wildcard — speed could be extraordinary or the surface transition could blunt it entirely.
runners_data.comment: Showed plenty of pace when winning by five lengths on debut at Woodbine, and the step into this 21-runner field from stall 3 is a neutral factor; first-time blinkers could sharpen the focus, though whether she sees out the trip under 126 lb remains the key question.

runners_data.name: Fanshell Beach
runners_data.note: Second Wesley Ward runner, James McDonald aboard and 53 days since last ran suggesting a degree of freshness targeted at this race; going flag is UNKNOWN for British turf, and the unknown style tag means tactical positioning is entirely speculative — monitor for early move from the gates.
runners_data.comment: Impressive on debut at Churchill Downs — winning by 5¼ lengths despite a slow start — Fanshell Beach arrives from stall 11 carrying 126 lb with first-time blinkers as the stable's second string, and while our rating of 115 underlines the form, stamina for this longer trip remains the key question.

runners_data.name: Through The Years
runners_data.note: The most experienced of the Ward trio with a form string of 2-1, John Velazquez aboard — the veteran American jockey gives this runner the best chance of positioning itself correctly early in an unfamiliar environment; going is flagged UNKNOWN for British turf but the presence of a win and a place on the form card makes this the Ward runner to respect most.
runners_data.comment: Backed up a debut run with a convincing Fillies & Mares victory at Belmont last time, and acts well on firm ground, but stable form has taken a few knocks this week and first-time blinkers add an element of the unknown for this stall-15 runner.

races.paceDynamic: Where Love Lives is the one confirmed front-runner in this 21-runner field and, with Kevin Stott in the saddle, will stride out from the gates and attempt to control the pace from the front on Good To Firm ground at Ascot — a track where five-furlong races are genuinely flat and time-honest, meaning an uncontested leader can dictate fractions comfortably. The key tactical reality is that this field is saturated with naturally prominent horses — Social Symbol, Orthodox, Flight Signal, El Floridita, Persian Spring, Carry The Flag and others all want to race handily — but only a handful can actually occupy those berths in a 21-runner sprint, meaning a large number of prominent types will be squeezed out of their natural positions and forced to race in a more restrained manner than ideal. With Where Love Lives likely to secure a clear lead without being seriously harassed, the pace will be honest but controlled rather than breakneck, producing a race that sets up well for horses who can travel prominently in the first two or three positions and sustain their effort all the way to the line — true, natural prominent racers who actually secure their position early are the dominant profile to favour here.

watchPoints.text: Where Love Lives is the only true front-runner in a 21-runner field — if Kevin Stott gets a clear lead in the first furlong, the race shape is set and everything else is chasing; watch the first 100 yards closely to see if any rival genuinely contests the lead.

The Ward trio (Ez Tina, Fanshell Beach, Through The Years) are going-unknown wildcards — if any one of them breaks sharply and burns up to challenge Where Love Lives, it transforms the entire pace dynamic and could compromise every horse racing prominently.

races.name: Hardwicke Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Amiloc
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old showed smart form when winning at 1m4f on good ground but his most recent run — a disappointing sixth — will need a convincing explanation; his true racing position is up with the pace, though the field's numerical dominance of prominent types means he is likely to be racing at slightly less than his natural pitch, a factor that could blunt his effectiveness here.
runners_data.comment: Won the King Edward VII Stakes here last year, but pulled hard and faded when too fresh at York last time (36 days ago); with that run now in the tank a revival is plausible, though ranked 9 of 12 on our figures this looks a notably stronger test.

runners_data.name: Best Secret
runners_data.note: The French raider won his last two at 1m2f on heavy/soft ground and his lone good-ground run of note resulted in a second — the surface is not a concern, but good-to-firm may be faster than ideal; Stuart Wattel's horse naturally wants to race prominently, and being crowded into a slightly deeper berth by the traffic ahead could interrupt the rhythm that underpins his best form.
runners_data.comment: Thriving form — three wins in its last five starts, the most recent a convincing Group 3 success at Longchamp — but Best Secret returns after 48 days and steps up markedly in class; the galloping track suits a big, progressive type, though the 129 lb burden is a genuine test.

runners_data.name: Ethical Diamond
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins sends out this six-year-old gelding wearing a hood, and his form at 1m4f-1m6f on good ground is solid; McMonagle takes over in the saddle, but a wide-margin defeat on his most recent run at Royal Ascot 84 days ago needs to be explained — his Group 1 winning form at 1m2f suggests he is better at a shorter trip, making the stamina test here a question mark.
runners_data.comment: Wearing a hood for the first time and back after 84 days, Ethical Diamond's Dubai reappearance — beaten 6½ lengths — is best set aside given that progressive C&D-winning profile, yet our figures rank this 11th of 12 and a career-best effort may be required.

runners_data.name: Giavellotto
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's seven-year-old is a model of consistency, placing in 8 of 10 similar-ground starts, but his win record is thin at this level — only one success in his last five — and Oisin Murphy will need to find a passage quickly turning for home given how crowded the prominent group is likely to be; his ceiling looks more like a placed effort than a winning one.
runners_data.comment: Consistent, well-travelled performer and former Hong Kong Vase winner, Giavellotto was 4¼ lengths back in third last time at Group 1 level, running his race without troubling the best — 84 days off could blunt his edge, though a top jockey returns and he handles today's conditions.

runners_data.name: Goliath
runners_data.note: The French raider brings a tidy record of three wins from five starts on good ground including his most recent success, and Christophe Soumillon will be intent on sitting prominently given the horse's natural style; a 20-day turnaround is short but Graffard has used that freshen-up approach before, and Goliath's consistency at 1m2f raises a mild question over whether 1m4f stretches his stamina at this class.
runners_data.comment: Twice a G1 winner and a former C&D scorer now back to his best, Goliath arrives on the back of a comfortable Group 2 success 20 days ago — form figures reading 1-2-3 in his last three — and handles today's distance and going well; the worry is that one rival has matched him closely in recent encounters.

runners_data.name: Jan Brueghel
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner at OR 123, he is the sole confirmed front-runner and with Ryan Moore on board he is almost certain to control the tempo; his 14-day turnaround is workable given he runs for Aidan O'Brien's strong yard, and his winning form at 1m4f on good ground directly suits — the only caveat is whether his Grade-mapped role as the field's pace-setter makes him vulnerable when he flattens late.
runners_data.comment: Dual-distance winner and St Leger champion in 2024, Jan Brueghel arrives on a 14-day turnaround with a proven jockey aboard and connections who have a strong record in this race — though the testing ground that cost him dearly at Epsom last time remains the key concern.

runners_data.name: Lambourn
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's four-year-old has five wins in his last seven starts — a standout figure on paper — but his recent wins came at 1m and 1m2f; shown at the back of the field by redistribution despite being a naturally prominent runner, Wayne Lordan will likely be uncomfortable with that position, and the combination of trip uncertainty and an artificial starting slot makes him difficult to assess with confidence.
runners_data.comment: Placed at the top level and a proven Group 1 winner over course and distance, Lambourn arrives 14 days after being sent into an overly prominent position in the Coronation Cup, paying for it with a 16-length defeat; first-time cheekpieces and a tempered approach may help, but the 129 lb burden and signs of awkwardness suggest this is likely the stable's supporting act.

runners_data.name: Phantom Flight
runners_data.note: George Scott's seven-year-old has an admirable win record at 1m-1m2f on good ground but jumps up sharply in class and distance here; his naturally prominent racing style is squeezed back by the busy field, which is a structural disadvantage, and his OR of 110 is the joint-lowest in the race — he requires career-best form to feature.
runners_data.comment: Beaten comfortably in a Group 3 on its latest start, Phantom Flight may still need time to re-acclimatise after a Middle East campaign and, ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, is hard to fancy despite a trainer in form and proven stamina at this trip and going.

runners_data.name: Sons And Lovers
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's five-year-old has strong stamina credentials — three wins over 1m3f-1m7f on good ground — but his last four finishes have all been thirds or fourths, suggesting he runs up to his level without quite winning; naturally a handy horse, his enforced position further back in a congested field reduces his ability to influence the race from the front half.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces go on for the first time here, and Sons And Lovers does boast a couple of wins in its last five starts — but two consecutive fourths, including an eight-length beating in a Group 3 latest, suggest this step into deeper waters is a tough ask, ranking last on our figures.

runners_data.name: West Wind Blows
runners_data.note: William Buick's partner has a striking record of 9 places from 11 similar-ground runs but zero wins in that sample, suggesting a horse that runs consistently without delivering the decisive change of gear required to win at this level; mapped to the rear despite a naturally prominent style, he will need the pace to collapse ahead of him for his relentless galloping to translate into a victory.
runners_data.comment: Desperately consistent at the top level, West Wind Blows went agonisingly close in a Group 3 at Newbury last time, going down by a neck, and acts on any ground over this trip; the concern is that a couple of today's rivals have finished ahead of him lately.

runners_data.name: Kalpana
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's five-year-old mare arrives in the best recent form in the race, having won her last two including a Listed success at 1m2f on good ground; she carries 126lbs and Colin Keane rides, and her high cruising speed means she can travel comfortably just off Jan Brueghel without needing a frenetic gallop to bring her finish into play — her going record of 9 from 15 similar-ground runs confirms the surface is no issue.
runners_data.comment: Kalpana arrives here in back-to-back winning form, including a G1 success over course and distance, and a narrow Group 3 victory last time that came despite racing a touch keenly and feeling the run close home — both concerns now resolved; first-time cheekpieces on a top-class filly who may still have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Santorini Star
runners_data.note: William Haggas has this five-year-old in fine form — two wins from his last four including a success at 1m4f — and Tom Marquand has ridden him before; he wears a hood and his record of 4 wins and 4 places in 13 similar-ground starts shows he handles the surface, but his natural urge to race prominently will be tempered by the quantity of horses ahead of him, leaving him likely to be shuffled wider for room.
runners_data.comment: Santorini Star arrives in cheekpieces for the first time off a solid run — beaten a short-neck at Group 1 level last time — and clearly has upward momentum over 12-16f on any surface, but this sharper trip may just stretch its speed reserves against stronger company.

races.paceDynamic: Jan Brueghel is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with Ryan Moore in the saddle, is likely to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over 1m4f at Ascot — a track that rewards horses who travel well through a race rather than those who need a searching pace to bring them into it. With no genuine rival willing to press him hard for the lead, Moore can set his own fractions, conserve energy through the middle sections, and ask his mount to stretch turning for home, giving Jan Brueghel the classic advantage of a front-runner who is never forced to work. This field is saturated with prominent-racing types — Amiloc, Best Secret, Santorini Star, Sons And Lovers, Phantom Flight, Goliath, Ethical Diamond, and Giavellotto all naturally want to race handy, meaning the race shape is compressed and mid-pack positions will be congested with horses racing out of their preferred spots, which further reduces the ability of genuine closers to generate momentum from deep. The redistribution of so many prominent types into artificially deeper slots means the horses who can travel smoothly just off the pace in a genuine position — rather than those shunted back — will be best served; this race shape strongly favours horses with high cruising speeds who sit within striking distance of Jan Brueghel, rather than hold-up operators relying on late acceleration that may never arrive.

watchPoints.text: Jan Brueghel and Ryan Moore — if Moore is allowed to bowl along uncontested on the front end, the winning margin could be significant and any horse that lets the gap grow beyond two lengths turning for home will find it hard to recover.

Kalpana's draw and early positioning — Colin Keane must ensure she settles just off Jan Brueghel without getting boxed in by the cluster of prominent types; any scrimmaging in the first furlong as multiple horses seek the same real estate could disrupt her rhythm.

Goliath's stamina at 1m4f — his best form is over 1m2f and while he handles good ground well, if Moore puts in a brisk middle mile Soumillon may find his mount emptying in the final furlong rather than staying on.

Traffic risk between the three-furlong and two-furlong marks — with so many horses naturally prominent and compressed into a tight mid-race group, the home straight at Ascot could see significant checking and switching, creating a lottery for horses like Santorini Star and Giavellotto who need a clear run.

Best Secret's ground preference — his two most recent wins came on heavy ground in France; good-to-firm is markedly faster and connections will know quickly after the first two furlongs whether he is travelling with the fluency that his best form requires.

races.name: Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Almeraq
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner with a sharp recent form string (1-F-1-2-1) carrying strong Good-ground course form; a natural prominent racer whose tactical speed means it will be pressing forward regardless of its mapped rearward position — Haggas horses tend to be produced with purpose and Tom Marquand will be looking to steal a march.|
runners_data.comment: Took the Cathedral Stakes (Listed) at Salisbury by a neck on most recent start 28 days ago, confirming current form, and handles this trip and going well — though fast conditions remain an unknown and there's still a gap to bridge at this level from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Aramram
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's five-year-old has Group-level experience at 6f and ran well in similar company earlier in the season; he's a front-end type by nature who will be squeezed rearward by the sheer volume of pace here, meaning Sean Levey must ride a different race to his instinct.|
runners_data.comment: Proven at course and distance and has performed creditably at Group level — including a solid third-placed effort in a Group 2 last time — but ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, and stepping into this grade makes this a considerably stiffer challenge than anything faced before.

runners_data.name: Comanche Brave
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien yard in modest 14-day form but the horse arrives on the back of a 6f Good-ground win; he wants to be prominent and will race aggressively, though in a field this size Boudot will likely find himself three or four off the pace rather than where he'd choose to be.|
runners_data.comment: Landed the Greenlands Stakes (Group 2) at The Curragh on latest start, quickening clear by two lengths, and has run well at this course before — but ranked 15th of 19 on our figures, making a step up to Group 1 level a tall order at 131lb.

runners_data.name: Great Wish
runners_data.note: Danish-trained Bent Olsen raider with a 6f Good-ground win on the board; 84 days off the track is the key question, and having been absent since spring he will need to find his rhythm quickly — a natural front-runner who must settle for a cramped position in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Stepped up to Group 1 company last time, Great Wish was beaten just over two lengths at Meydan — respectable enough, but ranked 17th of 19 on our figures, this looks a tough ask again; the 84-day break and proven effectiveness over 6f on good ground are the main positives.

runners_data.name: Jasour
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for Clive Cox and Rossa Ryan, wearing a hood; his last six runs on Good ground have produced finishes of 6-6-2-6-6 so the surface form is patchy, and he needs a genuinely hot pace to deliver his late run — the controlled tempo here is a structural negative.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and on a two-year losing run, Jasour faces a stiff task from stall 17 carrying 131 lb, and he often races keenly when his ideal conditions — 6f on fast ground — aren't fully met. First-time headgear is at least worth watching.

runners_data.name: Khaadem
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran for Charles Hills, one of only two genuine hold-up types in the field; Soumillon takes over and the horse's best form has come on Firm ground (1-3 on Firm, 9-10 last time on Soft), so the Good to Firm conditions are mildly encouraging but a solo closer in a 19-runner sprint field faces a stiff ask.|
runners_data.comment: Landed this prize in both 2023 and 2024, but disappointed on easy ground at Haydock last time out and needs a firm surface to show his best — conditions today are therefore key, and 131lb is a stiff burden if he's still finding his feet.

runners_data.name: Kind Of Blue
runners_data.note: William Buick and James Fanshawe combination; the horse has a clear pattern of performing well at 6f on Good ground and finished second in this race last year — he is a natural prominent runner who should actually secure that position here, and his consistency in this grade makes him a cornerstone of Scenario A.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent sort who has shown good form on the comeback trail, finishing second on latest outing at York in a Group 2, beaten a length; yet to win in recent starts, and the 131 lb burden is a stern ask, though acts on any ground and is proven at today's trip.

runners_data.name: Lake Forest
runners_data.note: William Haggas's best hope and the highest-rated runner in the field at OR 119; Cieren Fallon takes the ride, and the horse has Group-race form at 7f and 8f suggesting he may be stepping back in trip — but his 6f win last time out on Good confirms he can be effective, and he should secure a prominent pitch in running.|
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to form with a dominant Listed success at Haydock last time, beating rivals by five and a half lengths, and handles today's trip and fast surface well; the main risk is whether a 42-day break takes the edge off that sharp comeback.

runners_data.name: Lugal
runners_data.note: Japanese raider for Sugiyama, carrying good recent form (1-2-3); 84 days off and the switch from Japanese conditions to a competitive Ascot sprint are the risks — he is a genuine prominent runner with strong Good-ground course form (15 runs on Good, three wins) and Sameshima will aim to hold a stalking position.|
runners_data.comment: Placed in a Group 1 Al Quoz Sprint last time out, beaten a neck, and effective at this trip on a sound surface — the form profile has genuine merit — but our figures rank Lugal well down the field, and a Japanese Grade 1 winner in strong form makes further progress essential.

runners_data.name: Overpass
runners_data.note: Australian seven-year-old for Bjorn Baker, arriving just four days after his last run; his sprint form on Good ground is solid (2-3 in recent European runs) and Joshua Parr should be able to place him handily — the very short turnaround is the only concern.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who did plenty of the donkey work when a creditable third in a Group 1 here just four days ago, and that quick turnaround is an obvious concern; a proven G1 performer over this trip and going, though this stiff straight may not play to his prominent style.

runners_data.name: Powerful Glory
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey four-year-old with back-to-back 6f Good-ground wins; Jamie Spencer's waiting style often means he drops in but this horse races prominently by nature — one of the likelier candidates to actually hold a forward berth.|
runners_data.comment: Group 1 winner over course and distance in the autumn, Powerful Glory arrives here 28 days on from a reappearance defeat that should have put an edge on fitness — the main risk is that seventh last time out proves harder to excuse than it looks.

runners_data.name: Regional
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's durable eight-year-old, wearing a hood; he has extraordinary consistency at 6f on Good ground with 14 career runs at this trip, and Callum Rodriguez knows him well — though crammed into the midfield by the pace surplus, his form reads better than his mapped position suggests.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in recent starts, Regional at least showed consistency when finishing a close third in a Group 2 at York on its comeback 38 days ago, suggesting fitness isn't an issue. First-time headgear and stall 2 are noted, but stepping up in class looks the main obstacle here.

runners_data.name: Sajir
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners this A Fabre runner, which won a 6f Good-ground Listed race last time and has solid Soft-ground form too; he arrives fresh on 20 days and with strong recent form (1-2-2-1), and Murphy's positioning instinct should help him secure a forward slot.|
runners_data.comment: Sajir brings a live profile into this: a Group 3 winner last time at Chantilly and a Group 1 scorer over this trip last term, with a trainer in good heart and 20 days' rest suggesting peak fitness. The step back up in distance suits, though the 131 lb burden is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Satono Reve
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on the confirmed front-runner; the horse has strong Good-ground form at 6f at Ascot (2-1 in his last two visits) and wearing a hood — Moore is likely to manufacture a lead that is firm enough to be sustainable but controlled enough to give him a fight in the final furlong, and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects the structural question of whether he can hold 18 rivals off.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten just over four lengths when second in a Group 1 at Sha Tin last time, this multiple G1 winner from Japan was arguably unlucky in this same race twelve months ago. First-time headgear adds intrigue, though 55 days off the track is the one query.

runners_data.name: Stolen Kiss
runners_data.note: French filly for P Cottier who has won her last three starts including on Soft and Heavy; she is a natural front-runner wearing a hood, but her going form is all soft-ground and she has no confirmed Good-to-Firm form in her history — Pouchin will be seeking a forward spot she is unlikely to find in this congested field.|
runners_data.comment: Progressive dual Listed winner whose three recent victories show sharp current form, but at 131lb from stall 15 wearing a first-time tongue-tie on ground that may not suit, this 47-day absence makes it hard to confidently oppose our bottom-ranked figure here.

runners_data.name: Flora Of Bermuda
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's five-year-old filly won a 6f handicap at Ascot last time and arrives in good form; James Doyle takes the ride and she is a natural front-end type, though the step into Group 1 company and the redistribution rearward in this pack are clear challenges.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent strong traveller who landed a Listed prize at Newmarket on her latest start, though that came 49 days ago and ninth-place effort beforehand clouds the picture slightly; handles today's trip and conditions well, and connections have a strong record at this track.

runners_data.name: Joliestar
runners_data.note: Chris Waller's mare has won three straight including two on Good ground; James McDonald is one of the best sprint riders in the world and she is on a career-high trajectory — she should actually secure a forward berth and the form makes her one of the more serious threats here.|
runners_data.comment: Three wins on the bounce, including a hard-fought Group 1 victory at Randwick last time, underline Joliestar's outstanding recent form, and a weight advantage over the chief dangers adds further appeal for a yard with a strong record at this track.

runners_data.name: Sayidah Dariyan
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's four-year-old filly, ridden by Billy Loughnane; she won a 6f handicap on Good ground but has been well beaten in similar company this season, and in a field this deep a natural prominent racer being pushed towards midfield faces the double disadvantage of traffic and an unfamiliar role.|
runners_data.comment: Third on return to Listed level at Newmarket 49 days ago, Sayidah Dariyan clearly thrives at this course and distance on fast ground, and that run should leave her sharper — though stepping back up to this grade makes life considerably harder from stall 19.

runners_data.name: Time For Sandals
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's four-year-old filly runs just four days after her last outing; her form figures at 6f on Good ground are modest (19th, 8th, 5th, 7th) and she is another prominent type forced rearward by the pace surplus — the short turnaround and limited 6f Good-ground form make this a tough ask.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score since taking the Commonwealth Cup over this course and distance last year, Time For Sandals has largely toiled since, most recently beaten six lengths in a Group 1 here after being pushed along too prominently — a quick four-day turnaround makes things no easier from stall 16.

races.paceDynamic: Satono Reve is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 19, and with Ryan Moore in the saddle he is likely to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than an honest burning pace — creating a single-file procession rather than a genuine speed duel. Behind him, Kind Of Blue, Lake Forest, Sajir, Joliestar, Lugal, Overpass and Powerful Glory are all genuine prominent-racers who will press for early position in the first two furlongs, generating significant jostling for the first three or four berths and producing a race that is fast enough to test stamina but not a true lung-bursting test. The result is a race shape where those who can travel comfortably in the first two or three positions — or who can quicken off a steady-to-brisk tempo — have a clear structural advantage; this is a prominent-racer's race on a flat, Good to Firm Ascot 6f straight, and hold-up horses face the dual problem of traffic in a big field and a tempo that may not stretch the front runners enough. This field holds considerably more prominent types than the map can accommodate in their natural position: Comanche Brave, Regional, Flora Of Bermuda, Stolen Kiss, Great Wish, Aramram, Almeraq, Time For Sandals and Sayidah Dariyan are all natural prominent/pressing types who are most likely to find themselves shuffled towards midfield at the start — those best placed to actually secure prominent berths are Kind Of Blue, Lake Forest, Sajir, Joliestar and Powerful Glory, who are the class runners with the tactical speed and jockey quality to assert early.

watchPoints.text: Satono Reve's early lead is the fulcrum of the race — if Kind Of Blue or Sajir go with Moore immediately, the gallop accelerates and the whole pace scenario shifts; watch the first two furlongs to see whether Moore faces a genuine challenge or sails clear uncontested.

Joliestar is a three-race winner in flying form with James McDonald aboard — if she secures a prominent position as expected, she is capable of sustaining that speed all the way to the line and could outrun her odds.

Lake Forest steps back from 7f-8f to 6f and is one of the highest-rated in the field — if Cieren Fallon is able to slot him in behind the leader without burning his engine, he represents the primary danger to any front-end winner.

The 19-runner field on a straight 6f at Ascot creates significant draw and traffic risks — horses drawn wide or shuffled sideways in the opening furlong could lose multiple lengths before the race settles; Overpass (4 days ago) and Time For Sandals (4 days ago) both have the additional factor of very quick turnrounds.

Stolen Kiss's entire winning form is on Soft or Heavy ground — if there is any evidence during the meeting that the track is riding faster than soft, connections and punters should be alerted to the going concern before she runs.

races.name: Jersey Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Dorset
runners_data.note: Progressive Aidan O'Brien three-year-old with course-going form (5/8 on similar), but a natural prominent racer who is likely to find himself shuffled into a midfield position he doesn't want in this traffic-heavy field; discount accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just 6½ lengths in a Group 1 on its latest start, Dorset has solid credentials at this trip and should take to quick ground, though at 132 lb against likely improvers, a top-three finish may prove beyond a horse whose recent string suggests Group 3 level.

runners_data.name: Thesecretadversary
runners_data.note: Two wins on good ground and genuine pace, placed six times in eight runs; well suited by this 7f trip and likely to sit just off the leader in a proper prominent berth, making him a live each-way contender.
runners_data.comment: Held up without room at a crucial point in the Irish 2,000 Guineas last time, Thesecretadversary shaped better than a sixth-place finish suggests; a Group winner proven on today's going and a clear class edge dropping in grade makes this the one to beat from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Andab
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter for Joseph O'Brien with visor worn, but this horse's natural instinct is to race close to the pace — in a field this deep with prominent types, he will likely be outpaced for position and run from further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without ever quite winning the argument at this level, Andab steps up in a visor for the first time from stall 12 carrying 129 lb, and while the mile trip and ground hold no fears, a 6-length third in Listed company last time out underlines both the solid form and the ceiling.

runners_data.name: Ardisia
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer three-year-old who has raced prominently but recent form includes a run over 8f on Firm ground where she dropped away; this field size may see her bumped further back than she'd like, dulling her effectiveness.
runners_data.comment: Ran to form when a close-up third in Listed company on her latest start 15 days ago, and handles today's trip and conditions, though she may be best over a shorter six furlongs. Yet to win in her last five starts and carries 129 lb from stall 15.

runners_data.name: Avicenna
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's lightly-raced sort with a 100% win record at 7f on good ground and two wins from four starts, but classified here as prominent and mapped to hold-up — natural positional instinct means any late finish is manufactured rather than natural.
runners_data.comment: Showed smart form earlier in the season with back-to-back wins, though the Craven form has taken a few knocks and a well-beaten effort in the 2000 Guineas last time out raises questions; stepping back from Group 1 company helps, but 49 days off and 129 lb from stall 16 add to the puzzle.

runners_data.name: Billecart
runners_data.note: Karl Burke's hold-up horse with just one good run on similar going in four recent starts; a genuine rear-runner in a field where the pace is unlikely to be truly severe, limiting the amount of ground he can make up.
runners_data.comment: Sent to post 49 days ago and dropped back in from a Group 1 mauling at Newmarket, Billecart's ceiling now looks fairly clear despite that earlier win; acts on the going and trip, but ranked 14 of 17 on our figures, this good-looking colt has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Catullus
runners_data.note: William Buick aboard a Charlie Appleby horse who won last time at 7f on good — a naturally prominent type who has been mapped to hold-up because of field congestion, but Buick is likely to push forward regardless; treat as a prominent runner.
runners_data.comment: Proven at today's trip and surface, and clearly thriving after wind surgery — that Goodwood win by four lengths on handicap debut was eyecatching, and there's a strong sense of more improvement to come. Dropping back after a 28-day break with 129 lb from stall 14, the step up in class is the key question.

runners_data.name: Colori Forever
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's course-form performer with back-to-back wins at 7f, but like several others here wants to be prominent and will find that position hard to claim in a 17-runner field; form profile is strong if he gets a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Hugely progressive with two wins in its last five starts — including a course success on this trip last time out — and clearly thriving, though a 43-day break and a tough 129 lb burden from stall 13 are factors to weigh against a step up in class.

runners_data.name: Into The Sky
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's progressive type who loves front-running and good ground, lightly raced and progressive over this trip; with Morris Dancer ahead, he may get a comfortable prominent spot and travel smoothly throughout.
runners_data.comment: Scored on the same distance and going combination on offer here, but that Group 1 fourth last time — beaten 12 lengths when ridden up with the pace on what may not have been the best ground — raises questions about stamina, and a further drop in trip may suit best.

runners_data.name: Morris Dancer
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's confirmed front-runner returning from 311 days off — the key pace figure in the race; if he retains his form from last season (two wins at 7f on good), the long layoff is the only question mark.
runners_data.comment: Carrying 129 lb from stall 8, Morris Dancer arrives on the back of a dominant Listed win at Salisbury with form since confirmed at Group level, suggesting there's more improvement to come at three — though 311 days off the track means this first run back may be needed.

runners_data.name: Neolithic
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes over on this A.P. O'Brien colt fitted with a hood; placed or winning at 7f on good ground twice in last six, progressive and should travel smoothly in the prominent group without overpressing.
runners_data.comment: Blinkers applied for the first time as Neolithic returns after 47 days, but this 107-rated runner sits 15th of 17 on our figures and must prove its soft-ground form translates on better going — a significant question mark. The top-grade jockey booking offers some hope.

runners_data.name: Saber Strike
runners_data.note: William Haggas's unbeaten two-from-two improver for Tom Marquand; both wins at 6-7f on good ground, the form is tight and compressed but the profile is compelling — naturally suited to the race shape this field creates.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back victories — the latest a Listed success at Newmarket — mark Saber Strike as a horse potentially operating above this level, with trainer form an added boost; the 50-day absence and a stiff 129 lb are the questions to answer from stall 9.

runners_data.name: Take Charge Star
runners_data.note: Murtagh-trained type who wears a tongue-tie and has struggled in recent form (5th, 8th), being a natural prominent racer unlikely to hold that position against classier pace rivals; step back to 7f after 8f runs may help.
runners_data.comment: Stepped up to Group 1 company last time and beaten over eight lengths, Take Charge Star faces a similarly stiff task here as our 17th-ranked runner; the first-time headgear is worth noting, and from stall 1 over a familiar trip, there's some optimism — but this looks a tough ask.

runners_data.name: America Queen
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's filly has won at 6f and placed twice at 7f on good — a clean, prominent profile and Billy Loughnane can likely slot her into a genuine tracking position; her proximity to the pace could be decisive.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a neck in a Group 3 on her latest start, America Queen has proven stamina for today's trip and handles this going, making her a genuine threat from stall 5 at 126 lb — though there's a question over whether she has more improvement to find.

runners_data.name: Domina Ignis
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's filly won at 6f on Standard but her two subsequent runs on good ground have been disappointing; a natural forwardly-placed type who is unlikely to find the prominent spot she needs against sharper rivals.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up well below her best in the 1000 Guineas last time, Domina Ignis faces a stiff task from stall 11 off 126 lb, and our figures rank her 13th of 17. The Fred Darling third showed genuine grit, and the mile trip is within range, but that Group 1 flop is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Green Sense
runners_data.note: James McDonald takes over for Joseph O'Brien; this horse won at 6f on soft and placed at 6f on good, but recent form suggests she needs more than this field will give — a natural prominent type whose redistribution to midfield reflects the race's congestion.
runners_data.comment: Blocked for a run when fifth in a Group 2 last time out, Green Sense has excuses but still needs to find plenty given a ranking of 16th in the field; acts on today's conditions and should stay the trip, so not without hope if returning to form.

runners_data.name: The Prettiest Star
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly is lightly raced but has won at 6f and placed at 7f on good ground; James Doyle in the saddle gives her tactical flexibility, and her profile — small field of starts, upward arc — fits a genuinely prominent role well.
runners_data.comment: Rockfel runner-up with Group 1 experience behind her, The Prettiest Star handles today's trip and conditions with authority and looks open to further progress — the 48-day absence is the one note of caution, though that Newmarket fourth suggests she returns in fine shape.

races.paceDynamic: Morris Dancer is the one confirmed front-runner in a field of 17 and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival who is likely to take him on — he should stride into an uncontested lead from the outset and control tempo at a rate that suits him on Good to Firm ground at Ascot. The bulk of this field is composed of prominent types: Thesecretadversary, Into The Sky, Neolithic, Saber Strike, America Queen and The Prettiest Star all want to race close to the pace and will jostle for early position just off the leader, creating a competitive but structured group rather than a truly burning gallop. With no horse likely to sprint past Morris Dancer in the early stages, the pace is likely to be honest rather than frenetic, setting up a strong-galloping, get-out-and-stay-prominent race shape rather than a slow-burn sprint finish. This race shape clearly favours horses who can travel prominently and produce a sustained gallop from two furlongs out — true hold-up horses are thin on the ground and those mapped to the rear (Catullus, Avicenna, Billecart) are natural prominent types displaced by the field's depth of pace runners, meaning their mapped position is artificial. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically all secure their natural position; Morris Dancer should lead unchallenged, with Into The Sky, Saber Strike, America Queen and The Prettiest Star the most likely to genuinely press into the prominent berths, while Dorset, Andab, Colori Forever, Green Sense and others will find themselves shuffled back against their instincts.

watchPoints.text: Morris Dancer returns from 311 days off as the race's only true front-runner — if he retains freshness and fitness, he controls the tempo and every scenario flows from him; monitor market moves for any stable confidence signals.

With at least six horses (Dorset, Andab, Colori Forever, Green Sense, Take Charge Star, Domina Ignis) all naturally wanting to race prominently but likely to be crowded out, early positional scrimmaging on the home straight bend could cause interference or knocked-back runners.

Catullus is mapped to hold-up but William Buick is renowned for pushing prominent types forward regardless of mapped position — if he drives to the front early, Morris Dancer's uncontested lead disappears and the pace scenario changes materially.

Saber Strike and The Prettiest Star share the most compressed, clean form profiles in the race — both unbeaten or near-unbeaten at this trip on this going — and both suit the dominant scenario; watch for them tracking the leader's quarters from the outset.

Avicenna's artificial mapping to hold-up masks a horse with a 100% record at 7f on good ground for Roger Varian — if Dawson manages to get him into a prominent position despite the redistribution, his class makes him dangerous in Scenarios A and B.

races.name: Wokingham Stakes (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Spy Chief
runners_data.note: Has the race to himself on the front end and William Buick will exploit that; four of last five on good ground and the lone leader role is ideal, though the STYLE_FIT tag suggests he rarely makes from the front and may idle once headed.
runners_data.comment: Placed when beaten a neck in a Listed race at Salisbury 28 days ago, Spy Chief is winless in his last five starts but that runner-up effort brings him close to his best; he handles today's trip and ground, though 7f could test his stamina, and he's run well at this track before.

runners_data.name: Soldier's Tree
runners_data.note: De Sousa booking for a horse who has won and placed consistently on good ground; only one similar-going run in last four is a mild concern but the 6f trip here suits and he travels prominently into races well.
runners_data.comment: Consistent profile here, with that Salisbury Listed third last time arguably flattering the bare figures given traffic issues — yet still carrying 137 lb off a mark of 107 leaves little room for manoeuvre, even if there's improvement to come at this trip on suitable ground.

runners_data.name: Run Boy Run
runners_data.note: Won two from three on good ground at this trip and distance, though the 84-day break and a visor worn last time add unknowns; prominent racer who needs to be close enough turning in on fast ground.
runners_data.comment: Scored narrowly in a Sprint Handicap at this mark three starts back before a poor latest effort, and first-time headgear plus a trainer in form add appeal — but 84 days off and a mark that may stretch him keep this a tentative each-way proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Double Rush
runners_data.note: Arrives in cracking form with back-to-back wins over this course and distance on good going; Shane Foley continues the partnership and the profile of a horse peaking into this race is compelling.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins — the latest a comfortable success at Newmarket off a mark 10lb lower than today's — mark Double Rush as the one to beat here, and a top course handler takes the reins on a horse still looking ahead of its current official rating despite the penalty.

runners_data.name: Mitbaahy
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type in a race that contains very few of them; Billy Loughnane takes off the penalty and the veteran showed a clean 6f win on good ground last season, but 84 days off and a tongue-tie add risk.
runners_data.comment: Fitness must prove itself after 84 days away, with recent outings — including a poor effort in the Cammidge Trophy — leaving wellbeing in question; yet Mitbaahy is effective over this trip on any ground, and a bounceback to his placed form would make him a live midfield contender from stall 27.

runners_data.name: Binhareer
runners_data.note: Haggas-trained four-year-old with a win and five placings at this trip, including a recent runner-up on good; Tom Marquand rides and the horse is course-and-distance reliable, with the prominent style suiting the likely race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a neck at York last time off a 5lb lower mark, Binhareer arrives here on the upgrade and looking capable of Listed/Group-level company, while a stiff track at today's trip plays to her strengths; 38 days between runs is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Two Tribes
runners_data.note: Won twice at 6f on good ground but hasn't run for 106 days and last two outings were disappointing; the hood helps focus but the form tails off when freshness wears thin.
runners_data.comment: Took a handicap by a short-head off this identical mark at Meydan in January, yet two unplaced efforts since suggest the handicapper has its measure, and 106 days off the track adds another question mark — albeit a form trainer and first-time headgear offer some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Heathcliff
runners_data.note: Won four of last five on standard or AW surfaces and holds only one run on good turf in recent history; the going record is a significant concern despite Cieren Fallon's quality and a prominent style that would otherwise fit.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way on a turf return in a Listed heat last time, Heathcliff looks to have plenty to prove on grass and sits at the foot of our rankings — though a winning profile over the trip and decent AW form provide slim crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Dubai Bling
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on a horse who has won at this exact trip on good going and is clearly progressive; prominent style perfectly suits the expected race shape and recent Ascot form reads well.
runners_data.comment: Touched off by a head last time out having encountered interference at a crucial point, Dubai Bling arrives in decent nick but carries 132lb from stall 23 in first-time cheekpieces, and a mark of 102 looks stiff for a horse our figures rank 25th of 28.

runners_data.name: Royal Zabeel
runners_data.note: Won on standard and has a decent Ascot record, but last four runs include some sizeable defeats; Jason Watson rides for Appleby and the prominent style suits, though the form line is inconsistent.
runners_data.comment: Listed winner in fair form and effective over today's trip on this going, Royal Zabeel brings solid credentials to stall 3 in a large field — though having found one too good for stamina close home when beaten two and a quarter lengths off this mark here last time, there are questions over whether it can go one better.

runners_data.name: Leovanni
runners_data.note: James McDonald is an eye-catching booking and the horse has won twice at 5f on good ground, but stepping up to 6f and a 119-day break are both genuine concerns alongside the tongue-tie.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in recent starts, Leovanni was making ground when hampered at Lingfield last time and shaped better than a two-length fourth suggests; a former Group winner now fitted with a tongue-tie returning from 119 days off, there's upside here if sharper for the break.

runners_data.name: Hammer The Hammer
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott rides for Kevin Ryan but the trainer has no wins in the last 14 days; went 14th on good ground last time and recent form at 6f has not translated — prominent racer who needs better than he has shown.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts but this second outing after a wind operation should see significant improvement — the York run was always about getting fit again. Capable of setting a strong pace over today's trip and going, though stall 7 may complicate that front-running style.

runners_data.name: Roman Dragon
runners_data.note: Horse flags a fade-in-finish warning, which is damning in a 6f sprint; Mason Paetel is a 5lb claimer and only 14 days since last run, although a win at 5f on good going hints at pace, it won't be enough if it weakens.
runners_data.comment: Narrowly got up at Chester three starts back off a 5lb lower mark, but has been out of the frame twice since and the 100 rating looks a stiff ask — ranked near the foot of our assessments, first-time visor added from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Flash Harry
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner who Rossa Ryan will attempt to push forward, but in a 28-runner field already carrying Spy Chief in the lead role, finding that position on a fast surface at Ascot is far from guaranteed; the h-hood worn recently acknowledges a tendency to get lit up.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with a hood for the first time and carrying 130 lb from stall 26, Flash Harry has course-and-distance form to call on and has shown he can bounce back after a flat outing — his Salisbury run last time may have been needed on quicker ground than ideal, but fast conditions today suit, and a return to winning form isn't out of the question.

runners_data.name: Fandom
runners_data.note: Recent winner on good ground and Sean Levey has placed him well before; naturally wants to race prominently but the redistribution note is honest — he is likely to find himself closer to midfield than his best form demands.
runners_data.comment: Thriving for a new yard after landing a Thirsk handicap last time, this US Listed winner arrives on a mark that still looks workable and has course-distance form to lean on, though that sixth in recent starts and a possible preference for faster ground give slight pause at 130 lb from stall 1.

runners_data.name: Far Above Dream
runners_data.note: Four wins at 6f on good going makes him statistically the most course-going-specialist in the race; Kieran Shoemark has a clear relationship with this horse, but his natural prominent style will be compromised by the sheer number of horses wanting the same real estate.
runners_data.comment: Progressive and course-loving, but ranked 23 of 28 on our figures and lugging 129 lb from stall 17 off a career-high mark makes this a tough ask, despite four wins in the last five starts and a tendency to keep finding improvement.

runners_data.name: Ten Pounds
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer is an interesting booking for a horse who wants to race prominently but will be pushed back; recent form at 5f and 6f has been mixed and the 21-day turnaround is fine, though the p-headgear hasn't consistently sparked improvement.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with cheekpieces for the first time, Ten Pounds shaped with real promise when runner-up by just half a length in a Carlisle Listed contest last time out, and looks fairly handicapped off a mark of 99 with today's longer trip an additional plus — he can carry his head awkwardly under pressure.

runners_data.name: Completely Random
runners_data.note: Won twice on all-weather but good-turf form is limited; Ryan Moore's quality is a factor, and the horse's natural prominent instinct will be tested by the crowded pace map — likely to find itself further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces fitted for the first time could spark the turnaround after being left with it all to do from the rear at this course last time; yet to be beaten for today's jockey and progressive on this surface, though two unplaced efforts in recent starts demand respect.

runners_data.name: Thunderbear
runners_data.note: One of the genuine hold-up types in the field; needs the pace to set up a finish and has won at 6f on good ground, but the 54-day break and a trainer with zero wins in 14 days temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Thunderbear has yet to hit its stride this season and comes into this ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, with an unplaced effort last time out doing little to inspire confidence. A proven performer over the trip on varying ground at least offers some encouragement after 54 days off.

runners_data.name: Candy
runners_data.note: Long absence of 259 days is a serious red flag even for a horse who won on soft going; Saffie Osborne is apprentice weight-claiming, but the form before the break faded badly and returning in a 28-runner Royal Ascot handicap is a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Took the Ayr Silver Cup by two lengths off a 6lb lower mark two starts back, but flopped in Listed company most recently and returns after a 259-day absence; the trainer is in good nick and this trip and ground suit, though Candy may need the run to find full stride.

runners_data.name: Fast Track Harry
runners_data.note: Won twice on standard surfaces and was placed on good last time; Clive Cox runs two in this race and Jack Nicholls takes the 5lb claim, but the natural prominent style will be displaced toward midfield in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 8¼ lengths at York last time after being sent to the front too soon, Fast Track Harry has since slipped to the bottom of the rankings despite two earlier wins in this sequence; he looks fully exposed to the assessor now, and first-time cheekpieces offer little obvious rescue from stall 21.

runners_data.name: Apollo One
runners_data.note: Christophe Soumillon is a big-race booking but this eight-year-old's recent form shows a series of mid-pack finishes on good and soft; only 14 days since last run and the 0W in similar going makes the hold-up profile here hard to see delivering.
runners_data.comment: Held every chance at Epsom 14 days ago but beaten five-plus lengths below form, leaving questions; yet to win in his last six starts, though the 2nd and 3rd suggest ability, his mark of 97 looks fair and he handles today's conditions.

runners_data.name: Evening Saigon
runners_data.note: Won twice on standard surfaces and twice on slow going, but good-ground form is limited to a single runner-up; the prominent style will be suppressed by the congested pace map and the stable's 14-day strike rate is modest.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces go on for the first time, and there is some encouragement in a neck second last time off a mark of 92 — though today's conditions see this lightly raced sort stepping up 5lb, and ranked 20 of 28 on our figures, the case for it is thin.

runners_data.name: Realign
runners_data.note: James Doyle rides for Haggas, who is in excellent form (12/51 in 14 days); two wins on good ground at this trip give hope but the horse's prominent instinct will be frustrated and the headgear (p) was worn when winning — unchanged here.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces did the trick at Carlisle 21 days ago when Realign won a handicap by 1¼l, but today's higher mark looks a stiff ask; acts on any turf ground over this trip and the trainer is firing at 37%, yet that 5lb rise in the official rating may take the edge off him.

runners_data.name: Toyotomi
runners_data.note: Tudhope partners a true hold-up type who won at 6f on soft ground and has shown positional versatility; only 13 days since last run but genuine closers are rare in this field, giving Toyotomi a modest edge among the late-finishers.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Goodwood handicap by a neck 13 days ago, dropping in class and getting a clear passage, and remains fairly treated on older French form — but ranked 22 of 28 on our figures, carrying 127 lb from stall 8 makes the task considerably stiffer here.

runners_data.name: Sondad
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason's claim reduces the weight and the horse won at 6f on soft last time; the prominent inclination will be pushed back in this shape and the going is likely to be faster than his best form, with the visor headgear adding a wildcard.
runners_data.comment: Sondad brings a recent win at Epsom on his side — taking a handicap by two lengths off a reduced mark — and a solid course record with proven versatility on the going, but ranked 21st of 28 on our figures, first-time headgear adds an unknown, and he faces a big field from stall 2 carrying 127 lb off a restored official mark of 97.

runners_data.name: Trefor
runners_data.note: Five wins and seven places at 6f on good ground make this horse statistically reliable at the trip in the conditions; a 7lb claimer (Toby Moore) is a concern in this grade but the consistent form profile is noted, even if prominent running style faces a crowded lane.
runners_data.comment: Showed a return to form when a staying-on fourth at Windsor 26 days ago, beaten three lengths off this same mark, but the official rating of 96 looks a stiff ask; effective at five-to-six furlongs on sound ground, though that late fade raises questions about lasting home.

runners_data.name: Caburn
runners_data.note: James Tate's four-year-old won at 6f and has good pedigree for the trip; Colin Keane is a strong booking but the horse has been beaten in last three outings including a first on good ground that disappointed, and the prominent style is in a very congested position.
runners_data.comment: Patchy recent form and a mark that looks tough to overcome are the main concerns, but first-time cheekpieces and a notable jockey booking add interest, and Caburn does handle this trip and going well enough to be competitive if producing a career-best.

races.paceDynamic: Spy Chief is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse inclined to lead in a 28-runner field, will be able to stride into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm from the outset — a genuinely sustainable gallop rather than a scorched-earth fractions race. The sheer density of prominent-profile horses (Double Rush, Binhareer, Dubai Bling, Soldier's Tree among others) means the early-to-middle portion of the race will be populated by a wall of horses travelling prominently just off the pace, which in a race of this size creates significant traffic and positional friction for those trying to make ground from behind. The field contains far more front-running and prominent types than can physically occupy those positions; Flash Harry, Fandom, Far Above Dream, Caburn, Realign, Completely Random and several others are natural prominent racers who will be shuffled into midfield against their instincts, blunting their effectiveness. This race shape — a controlled single leader, a dense prominent pack, and a host of reluctant hold-up types — strongly favours horses who genuinely race in the prominent-to-lead band and can travel into the race with cover off a sensible gallop, then produce a clean turn of foot in the final two furlongs.
